tools.name: SuggestPluginInstall
tools.description:
Render an inline card of plugins the user can add to claude.ai, taken from SearchPlugins results. The card handles all install UI; do not describe the plugins in text.

Offer one when the task is the kind a plugin could take over or make repeatable (deploys, reviews against a team process, or the ticket, data and document workflows a user's org may have packaged as plugins) and nothing enabled covers it; the user does not need to ask about plugins. Also when they ask for plugin recommendations. First call SearchPlugins with keywords drawn from the task, then pass the relevant results here: pluginId from each result's id, pluginName from its name, description as returned. Set trigger ('proactive' when you initiated this from task context, 'user_asked' when they asked). Use ListPlugins for plugins they already have.

After the card, continue the task. Example: "ship this to staging" and a deploy plugin that is not enabled → contextLabel "For your deploys".

Do NOT call this for one-off questions you can answer directly, when you are unsure a plugin would help, when SearchPlugins returned nothing relevant (then continue the task without mentioning the search), or if you already rendered a plugin or skill suggestion this conversation and the user didn't engage.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

schema.name: ToolSearch
schema.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__update_plan
tools.description:
Keep the task list the app shows under your latest message while you work. Every request that edits files or runs more than one command gets one (implement-and-test, investigate-then-fix, anything the user listed); only a single-command answer or pure conversation does not.

Never spend a message on this tool alone: send it IN THE SAME MESSAGE as another tool call (in parallel), so it costs no extra round trip.
- First call: with the VERY FIRST tool call of the turn, even one that only reads or lists files: {"items": [...]}, the whole plan in order, short imperative phrases (at most ~7 words, no numbering), the step you are starting "in_progress", the rest "pending". If you must look around first, make "Look at how X is set up" step one and refine the list once you know.
- Next step: {"advance": true} alongside the call that begins it (completes the in_progress step, starts the next pending one); after the last step, advance alongside wrap_up.
- Out of order: {"done": [2], "start": 4} (1-based).
- Plan changed, including right after the user interrupts or sends a new instruction mid-task: {"items": [...]} again, the new whole list, so the pinned list never shows an abandoned plan.
- Every {"items"} call says in "scope" what this request is to the session: "first_task" (nothing finished here yet); after that, "new_task" (unrelated work: it builds on nothing done, found or decided here) or "continuation" (everything else: anything a few tool calls settle, the next iteration, acting on what you just investigated or suggested, even if that work gets its own commit or PR; when unsure, this one). A "new_task" turn opens with a start_session offer and reaches this call only if the user chose Do it here.
Keep exactly one step in_progress while working and none when everything is done. Do not also write the plan as a numbered list in your message: the pinned list is the plan.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__wrap_up
tools.description:
Fill the "next step" box the app shows at the end of your turn: a two-or-three-sentence recap and, when this turn leaves the user a decision to make or a step to take, one question and buttons that answer it; a turn with nothing pending ends with the recap alone, and the app then draws no box. Call it once in EVERY turn in which you kept a task list, changed files, ran commands, or completed multi-step work: when this turn's work is done, before any closing message (it also checks off the task list; no closing update_plan is needed). Skip it for short answers, pure conversation, or a brief read-and-explain turn — a reply that names a follow-up is not brief: ask or propose it, and call this.

Your closing message is ordinary text right after this call, the last thing you say this turn: your answer to the user in full, which the recap never replaces. Never write it before this call, where it can reach the user cut to a short summary. The result says whether the box shows your question: ask in the message only a question it does not show.

Fields — recap and ask are said to the user, in the second person; a reply button's label is the user's words back to you:
- recap: what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified (for example: nothing committed, or not checked in the app). Two or three short sentences, about 40 words / 300 characters, in the project's own words. No recommendation here.
- ask (with actions, only when the next move is the user's call — a choice of approach, a go-ahead to fix, commit, push, post or send, an approval): just that ONE decision in one short sentence, never two joined by "and" ("Which fix first?"), with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give: your pick, actions[0], is drawn as the primary button. At most 100 characters.
Every field is a top-level parameter holding plain prose (actions: a JSON array); none contains markup or another field.

recap.description: Two or three short sentences to the user (≤300 chars): what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified. Its first sentence is the sidebar status. It must stand on its own, since it is also read away from the transcript and the box draws under anything you write after this call: never point at anything else in the conversation ("listed below", "see above", "in my message").

blocked.description: true when your work stops here until the user answers (the app marks the session as waiting on them); omit when the answer can wait.

action.description: An app action update_plan's result listed as available now, or one your own work this turn made available; anything else is refused, and one that stops being available later is dropped (as actions[0], with your ask and the other answers), so do not guess. Omit for a reply.

label.description: For a reply: the button text, 1–3 words (4 only when three cannot say it) / 24 characters — "Yes, fix 1", "Fix 2 instead", "Not now": a button, not a sentence. A click sends it to you as the user's answer. No leading / or !. Ignored for an app action (the app's own label is used).

actions.description: 1–2 buttons, recommendation first. They are answers to your ask: the first accepts your recommendation, and another is there only when it is a realistic alternative the user might pick instead — not a menu of everything you mentioned. When blocked is true, they are the most likely answers to your question. While Auto-fix is on for the session's PR, none offers to watch it, fix CI, resolve conflicts or address comments.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

name.description: Tool name (e.g. computer, navigate, find, form_input, read_page). browser_batch cannot be nested. A tabs_create's new tabId is only returned when the batch ends — load that tab in a later call.

input.description: That tool's input — same shape you'd pass when calling it directly. For computer items whose action is left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key or type, and for form_input items, include action_summary in the item's input, as you would when calling that tool directly.

actions.description: List of tool calls to execute sequentially. Example: [{"name":"computer","input":{"action":"left_click","ref":"ref_12"}},{"name":"computer","input":{"action":"type","text":"hello"}},{"name":"computer","input":{"action":"screenshot"}}]

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Code_iOS_Simulator__control
schema.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'press_key' presses a hardware key 'count' times: return, delete (backspace), an arrow, select_all, undo or redo (a key also hides the on-screen keyboard); 'set_appearance' switches the device to light or dark mode; 'appearance' says which it is in; 'set_keyboard' shows or hides the on-screen keyboard (it appears only while a text field has focus, and 'press_key' and 'text' hide it again); 'rotate' turns the device a quarter turn left or right ('direction'); take a 'screenshot' after it and tap in that screenshot's frame, however it comes back; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': absolute path (no ~) to the built .app bundle (e.g. /Users/me/Library/Developer/Xcode/DerivedData/MyApp-abc123/Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the simulator already attached, else the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

key.description: For 'press_key': the key or edit command to press.

count.description: For 'press_key': how many times to press it, 1 to 20 (default 1).

state.description: For 'set_keyboard': 'show' or 'hide' the on-screen keyboard. For 'set_appearance': 'light' or 'dark'.

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

IMPORTANT: Call read_me before your first show_widget call. Do NOT narrate or mention the read_me call to the user — call it silently, then respond as if you went straight to building the visualization.

loading_messages.description: 1–4 loading messages shown to the user while the visual renders, each roughly 5 words long. Write them in the same language the user is using. Use 1 for simple visuals, more for complex ones. If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. Pandemic growth model — NOT ['Simulating patient zero', 'Modeling the curve'] (documentary-narrator voice), YES ['Setting up the model', 'Running the calculation']. Cancer timeline — NOT ['Charting the battle ahead'], YES ['Laying out the stages']. If you have to ask whether it's serious, it is. Otherwise, have fun — reach for alliteration, puns, personification, wordplay, whatever lands in that language. Playful examples — revenue chart: ['Bribing bars to stand taller', 'Asking Q4 where it went']; kanban: ['Herding cards into columns', 'Dragging, dropping, not stopping'].

title.description: Short snake_case identifier for this visual. Must be specific and disambiguating — if the conversation has multiple visuals, this title alone should tell you which one is being referenced (e.g. 'q4_revenue_by_product_line' not 'chart', 'oauth_login_flow' not 'diagram'). Also used as the download filename, so no spaces or special characters.

widget_code.description: SVG or HTML code to render. For SVG: raw SVG code starting with <svg> tag, must use CSS variables for colors. Example: <svg viewBox="0 0 700 400" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">...</svg>. For HTML: raw HTML content to render, do NOT include DOCTYPE, <html>, <head>, or <body> tags. Use CSS variables for theming. Keep background transparent and avoid top-level padding. Scripts are supported but execute after streaming completes.

207	  | step hpl ho _ ih => obtain ⟨x, hx, ha⟩ := ih; exact ⟨x, hx, .step hpl ho ha⟩

209	/-- Under `WF3`, no place on the ownership chain of a usable place `p`, `p` included, is owned
210	through `p` (§40: an ownership cycle makes no place usable; §49.2: parts share the owner). -/
211	theorem not_ownedIn_chain {s : S3} (hw : WF3 s) {p q : Nat} (hp : s.Usable p)
212	    (hq : q = p ∨ Above s.P p q) : ¬ OwnedIn s.P p q := by
213	  intro h
214	  obtain ⟨x, hx, hqx⟩ := OwnedIn.above h
215	  have hpx : Above s.P p x := by
216	    rcases hq with rfl | hq
217	    · exact hqx
218	    · exact hq.trans hqx
219	  obtain ⟨plx, plp, hplx, hplp, ho⟩ := hw.ownerOf hx
220	  cases hpx with
221	  | owner hpl hpo =>
222	    rw [hplp] at hpl; cases hpl
223	    cases hp with
224	    | frame hpl' _ hpo' _ => rw [hplp] at hpl'; cases hpl'; rw [hpo] at hpo'; cases hpo'
225	    | place hpl' _ hpo' hu =>
226	      rw [hplp] at hpl'; cases hpl'; rw [hpo] at hpo'; cases hpo'
227	      exact not_above_self hu (.owner hplx (ho.trans hpo))
228	  | step hpl hpo hcx =>
229	    rw [hplp] at hpl; cases hpl
230	    cases hp with
231	    | frame hpl' _ hpo' _ => rw [hplp] at hpl'; cases hpl'; rw [hpo] at hpo'; cases hpo'
232	    | place hpl' _ hpo' hu =>
233	      rw [hplp] at hpl'; cases hpl'; rw [hpo] at hpo'; cases hpo'
234	      exact not_above_self hu (hcx.trans (.owner hplx (ho.trans hpo)))

236	/-! ## The shared preservation argument (§57, §69, §70) -/
237	
238	/-- Releasing authorities and marking places dead, then releasing the authorities whose holder
239	died, preserves `KInv` (§57), provided the death markers respect parts (§49.2), usable places keep
240	only valid former anchors (§52, §44), the root authorities of usable root places are kept (§49.7),
241	and `NoDangling` (§54) holds afterwards. -/
242	theorem releases_preserve {s s₁ : S3} (hk : KInv s) (hr : OnlyReleases s s₁)
243	    (hP : s₁.P = s.P) (hF : s₁.F = s.F) (hn : s₁.nF = s.nF)
244	    (hd : ∀ q, s₁.dead q = false → s.dead q = false)
245	    (hparts : ∀ (q : Nat) (pl : Place) (r : Nat), s.P[q]? = some pl → pl.parent = some r →
246	      s₁.dead r = s₁.dead q)
247	    (hD : ∀ q, s₁.Usable q → ∀ x ∈ s₁.D q, x ∈ s.D q)
248	    (hI3 : ∀ q, s₁.Usable q → ∀ x ∈ s₁.D q, (cleanup s₁).Active x)
249	    (hroot : ∀ (r i : Nat) (z : Authority) (pr : Place), RootPlace s.P r → s₁.Usable r →
250	      s.A[i]? = some z → z.active = true → z.origin = none → s.P[r]? = some pr →
251	      z.holder = pr.owner → (∀ l, l ∈ z.footprint ↔ l ∈ footprint s.P r) → s₁.A[i]? = some z)
252	    (hnd : WF3 (cleanup s₁) → NoDangling (cleanup s₁)) :
253	    KInv (cleanup s₁) := by
254	  obtain ⟨hw, ⟨⟨i1, i2, -, -⟩, hao, -⟩, haoh, -⟩ := hk
255	  have hc := hr.trans (cleanup_releases s₁)
256	  have cP : (cleanup s₁).P = s.P := hP
257	  have cF : (cleanup s₁).F = s.F := hF
258	  have hu : ∀ q, s₁.Usable q → s.Usable q :=
259	    fun q h => S3.Usable.mono hP (fun f hf => hF ▸ hf) hd h
260	  have hU := cleanup_usable s₁
261	  have hw' : WF3 (cleanup s₁) :=
262	    { frames := by
263	        show s₁.F ≠ [] ∧ s₁.F.Nodup ∧ ∀ f ∈ s₁.F, f < s₁.nF
264	        rw [hF, hn]; exact hw.frames
265	      places := fun q pl r hq hp => by
266	        rw [cP] at hq
267	        obtain ⟨pr, hpr, hlt, ho, -⟩ := hw.places q pl r hq hp
268	        exact ⟨pr, by rw [cP]; exact hpr, hlt, ho, hparts q pl r hq hp⟩
269	      owners :=
270	        ⟨fun q pl f hq ho => by
271	          show f < s₁.nF
272	          rw [hn]; exact hw.owners.1 q pl f (by rw [← cP]; exact hq) ho,
273	        fun q pl o hq ho => by
274	          rw [cP]; exact hw.owners.2.1 q pl o (by rw [← cP]; exact hq) ho,
275	        fun q hq => hq.frameOf⟩
276	      footprints := fun a x hx l hl => by
277	        obtain ⟨x₀, hx₀, -, -, e, -⟩ := hc.2 a x hx
278	        rw [cP]; exact hw.footprints a x₀ hx₀ l (e ▸ hl)
279	      origins := fun b y a hb ho => by
280	        obtain ⟨y₀, hy₀, -, e, -⟩ := hc.2 b y hb
281	        exact hw.origins b y₀ a hy₀ (e ▸ ho)
282	      rootChain := hw.rootChain.transport (by rw [cP]) (by rw [cP]) (fun a => by rw [hc.ancs])
283	        (fun a y' hy' => by obtain ⟨y, hy, -, -, e, -⟩ := hc.2 a y' hy'; exact ⟨y, hy, e⟩)
284	        (fun x z hz hzo => by
285	          obtain ⟨z', hz', -, e1, e2, -⟩ := hc.get' hz
286	          exact ⟨z', hz', e1.trans hzo, e2⟩)
287	      rootHeld := fun r hrp hur => by
288	        rw [cP] at hrp
289	        have hu₁ := (hU r).1 hur
290	        obtain ⟨i, z, pr, hz, za, zo, zm, hpr, hh, hf⟩ := hw.rootHeld r hrp (hu r hu₁)
291	        have hz₁ := hroot r i z pr hrp hu₁ hz za zo hpr hh hf
292	        have hlive : HolderLive s₁ z.holder := by
293	          rw [hh]; exact owner_live hu₁ (by rw [hP]; exact hpr)
294	        refine ⟨i, z, pr, ?_, za, zo, zm, by rw [cP]; exact hpr, hh, by rw [cP]; exact hf⟩
295	        rw [cleanup_get, hz₁]; simp [hlive]
296	      holders := fun a y hy ya => by
297	        obtain ⟨-, hl⟩ := cleanup_active hy ya
298	        exact (HolderLive.congr (s := s₁) (s' := cleanup s₁) rfl rfl rfl _).2 hl }
299	  refine kInv_of hw' ⟨⟨?_, ?_, ?_, i4_always _⟩, ?_, hnd hw'⟩ ?_
300	  · intro a b x y p hab hx hy xa ya xp yp hnab hnba
301	    obtain ⟨x₀, hx₀, m₁, -, f₁, -, a₁⟩ := hc.2 a x hx
302	    obtain ⟨y₀, hy₀, m₂, -, f₂, -, a₂⟩ := hc.2 b y hy
303	    rw [hc.ancs] at hnab hnba; rw [m₁, m₂]
304	    exact i1 a b x₀ y₀ p hab hx₀ hy₀ (a₁ xa) (a₂ ya) (f₁ ▸ xp) (f₂ ▸ yp) hnab hnba
305	  · intro b y a hb ho
306	    obtain ⟨y₀, hy₀, m₀, e, f₀, -⟩ := hc.2 b y hb
307	    obtain ⟨x₁, hx₁, hm, hsub⟩ := i2 b y₀ a hy₀ (e ▸ ho)
308	    obtain ⟨x', hx', mx, -, fx, -⟩ := hc.get' hx₁
309	    exact ⟨x', hx', by rw [m₀, mx]; exact hm, fun l hl => by rw [fx]; exact hsub l (f₀ ▸ hl)⟩
310	  · exact fun q hq x hx => hI3 q ((hU q).1 hq) x hx
311	  · intro q hq x hx
312	    have hq₁ := (hU q).1 hq
313	    refine (hc.effAnchorOK cP cF x _).2 ?_
314	    rw [S3.pframe_congr cP]
315	    exact hao q (hu q hq₁) x (hD q hq₁ x hx)
316	  · intro q hq x y' hx ya hh
317	    obtain ⟨y, hy, -, -, -, e, ea⟩ := hc.2 x y' hx
318	    refine (hc.effAnchorOK cP cF x _).2 ?_
319	    rw [S3.pframe_congr cP]
320	    exact haoh q (hu q ((hU q).1 hq)) x y hy (ea ya) (e.symm.trans hh)
321	
322	/-- Releasing authorities with the places unchanged, then releasing the authorities whose holder
323	died, preserves the auxiliary `KAux` (`RootHeldConv`, §40, §49.7): authorities with no origin keep
324	their footprint and holder. -/
325	theorem releases_preserve_kAux {s s₁ : S3} (ha : KAux s) (hr : OnlyReleases s s₁)
326	    (hP : s₁.P = s.P) : KAux (cleanup s₁) := by
327	  have hc := hr.trans (cleanup_releases s₁)
328	  exact RootHeldConv.transport ha hP fun x z' hx ho => by
329	    obtain ⟨z, hz, -, e1, e2, e3, -⟩ := hc.2 x z' hx
330	    exact ⟨z, hz, e1 ▸ ho, e2, e3⟩

345	  map_releases rfl fun y => by by_cases h : heldIn s.P p y.holder <;> simp [h]

354	with a holder live after `endUseS`. -/

357	    s.A[j]? = some z ∧ ¬ heldIn s.P p z.holder ∧ HolderLive (endUseS s p) z.holder := by
358	  obtain ⟨hz₁, hl⟩ := cleanup_active hz za
359	  rw [endUseS_get] at hz₁
360	  cases hy : s.A[j]? with
361	  | none => rw [hy] at hz₁; cases hz₁
362	  | some y =>
363	    rw [hy] at hz₁
364	    by_cases hh : heldIn s.P p y.holder
365	    · simp only [hh, Option.map_some, ↓reduceIte, Option.some.injEq] at hz₁
366	      subst hz₁; simp at za
367	    · simp only [hh, Option.map_some, ↓reduceIte, Option.some.injEq] at hz₁
368	      subst hz₁; exact ⟨rfl, hh, hl⟩

376	  have hx₀ : x ∈ s.D q := by

378	    · simp at hx
379	    · exact hx

381	  have hc := hpre.anchors q (List.mem_range.2 hq₀.lt) hq x hx
382	  unfold EndUseAnchorOK OptP at hc; rw [hy] at hc
383	  obtain ⟨hnh, -, hl⟩ := hc

387	authority on a leaf of a place that stops being usable is derived, and blocked by §69.2, or a
388	root, held by the owner of the root place of the leaf (`rootHeldConv_active`), which would stay

390	theorem EndFree.endUse_noDangling {k : K} {s : S3} {p : Nat} (hw : WF3 s) (hnd : NoDangling s)

401	  have hl₁ : ¬ (endUseS s p).Usable l := fun hu => hq (usable_of_part hw' hlq ((hU l).2 hu))
402	  cases hzo : z.origin with
403	  | some o =>
404	    have hacc := hpre.access j (List.mem_range.2 (lt_of_getElem? hz₀))

427	    have hr₁ : (endUseS s p).Usable r := usable_of_owner hpr hd (hh ▸ hlive)
428	    exact hl₁ ((hU l).1 (usable_of_partOf hw' (l + 1) l r (Nat.lt_succ_self l) hlr ((hU r).2 hr₁)))

430	/-- `endUse` preserves the kernel invariant `KInv` (§57) (O12, §69). -/

531	    o = .reject := by
532	  cases h with
533	  | ok hpre =>
534	    have hn := hpre.notPinned l (List.mem_range.2 (endingLeaf_lt hl)) hl
535	    rcases hpin with e | e
536	    · rw [hn.1] at e; cases e
537	    · exact absurd e hn.2
538	  | reject _ => rfl

541	theorem endUse_det {k : K} {p : Nat} {s : S3} {o₁ o₂ : Outcome3 S3}
542	    (h₁ : EndUseStep k p s o₁) (h₂ : EndUseStep k p s o₂) : o₁ = o₂ := Guarded.det h₁ h₂

547	    EndUseStep k p s (.ok s') ↔ EndUsePre k s p ∧ s' = endUseEff s p := Guarded.ok_iff

549	/-! ## O13 `free` (§70) -/
550	
551	/-- The authorities after `freeS` (§70, `ok` effect): those covering the released unit or held
552	within `p` are inactive. -/
553	theorem EndFree.freeS_get (s : S3) (p j : Nat) : (freeS s p).A[j]? = (s.A[j]?).map fun y =>
554	    if (∃ l ∈ y.footprint, FreedPlace s.P p l) ∨ heldIn s.P p y.holder then
555	      { y with active := false } else y := by
556	  simp [freeS]
557	
558	/-- `freeS` only releases authorities (§70, `ok` effect). -/
559	theorem EndFree.freeS_releases (s : S3) (p : Nat) : OnlyReleases s (freeS s p) :=
560	  map_releases rfl fun y => by
561	    by_cases h : (∃ l ∈ y.footprint, FreedPlace s.P p l) ∨ heldIn s.P p y.holder <;> simp [h]
562	
563	/-- A place usable after `freeS` was usable before (§70: the effect only adds death markers). -/
564	theorem EndFree.freeS_usable {s : S3} {p q : Nat} (h : (freeS s p).Usable q) : s.Usable q :=
565	  S3.Usable.mono (s := s) (s' := freeS s p) rfl (fun _ h => h)
566	    (fun q h => by simp only [freeS, Bool.or_eq_false_iff] at h; exact h.1) h
567	
568	/-- An active authority after `free p` (§70, `ok` effect): active before, covering no leaf of the
569	released unit, not held within `p`, with a holder live after `freeS`. -/
570	theorem EndFree.free_active {s : S3} {p j : Nat} {z : Authority}
571	    (hz : (freeEff s p).A[j]? = some z) (za : z.active = true) :
572	    s.A[j]? = some z ∧ ¬ ((∃ l ∈ z.footprint, FreedPlace s.P p l) ∨ heldIn s.P p z.holder) ∧
573	      HolderLive (freeS s p) z.holder := by
574	  obtain ⟨hz₁, hl⟩ := cleanup_active hz za
575	  rw [freeS_get] at hz₁
576	  cases hy : s.A[j]? with
577	  | none => rw [hy] at hz₁; cases hz₁
578	  | some y =>
579	    rw [hy] at hz₁
580	    by_cases hc : (∃ l ∈ y.footprint, FreedPlace s.P p l) ∨ heldIn s.P p y.holder
581	    · simp only [hc, Option.map_some, ↓reduceIte, Option.some.injEq] at hz₁
582	      subst hz₁; simp at za
583	    · simp only [hc, Option.map_some, ↓reduceIte, Option.some.injEq] at hz₁
584	      subst hz₁; exact ⟨rfl, hc, hl⟩
585	
586	/-- The place released by `free` is a root place (§70.1, `OwnedRoot`). -/
587	theorem EndFree.rootPlace_of_ownedRoot {s : S3} {p : Nat} (h : OwnedRoot s p) : RootPlace s.P p := by
588	  unfold OwnedRoot OptP at h
589	  split at h
590	  · rename_i pl hpl; exact ⟨lt_of_getElem? hpl, by simp [parentOf, hpl, h.1]⟩
591	  · exact h.elim
592	
593	/-- A part of a root place `r` is a part of `p` exactly when it is `p` or its structural parent is
594	a part of `p`, for `p` a root place (§40). -/
595	theorem EndFree.partOf_parent {P : List Place} {q r p : Nat} (hp : parentOf P q = some r)
596	    (hlt : r < q) (hr : r < P.length) (hroot : parentOf P p = none) :
597	    partOf P q p ↔ partOf P r p := by
598	  have hq : q < P.length := by
599	    simp only [parentOf] at hp
600	    cases h : P[q]? with
601	    | none => rw [h] at hp; cases hp
602	    | some _ => exact lt_of_getElem? h
603	  simp only [partOf, hq, hr, true_and]
604	  rw [chain_cons hp hlt]
605	  constructor
606	  · rintro (rfl | h)
607	    · rw [hroot] at hp; cases hp
608	    · rcases List.mem_cons.1 h with rfl | h
609	      · exact .inl rfl
610	      · exact .inr h
611	  · rintro (rfl | h)
612	    · exact .inr (List.mem_cons_self ..)
613	    · exact .inr (List.mem_cons_of_mem _ h)
614	
615	/-- A root place that is a part of `p` is `p` (§40). -/
616	theorem EndFree.eq_of_partOf_root {P : List Place} {r p : Nat} (hr : RootPlace P r)
617	    (h : partOf P r p) : r = p := by
618	  obtain ⟨-, e | hc⟩ := h
619	  · exact e
620	  · rw [chain_none hr.2] at hc; simp at hc
621	
622	/-- Under `FreePre` (§70.3) and `I3` (§52), every anchor of a place usable after `freeS` stays
623	active after `free`. -/
624	theorem EndFree.free_anchors {k : K} {s : S3} {p auth : Nat} (h3 : I3 s) (hpre : FreePre k s p auth) :
625	    ∀ q, (freeS s p).Usable q → ∀ x ∈ (freeS s p).D q, (freeEff s p).Active x := by
626	  intro q hq x hx
627	  have hq₀ := freeS_usable hq
628	  obtain ⟨y, hy, ya⟩ := h3 q hq₀ x hx
629	  have hc := hpre.anchors q (List.mem_range.2 hq₀.lt) hq x hx
630	  unfold FreeAnchorOK OptP at hc; rw [hy] at hc
631	  obtain ⟨hcov, hnh, hl⟩ := hc
632	  have hn : ¬ ((∃ l ∈ y.footprint, FreedPlace s.P p l) ∨ heldIn s.P p y.holder) :=
633	    fun h => h.elim hcov hnh
634	  exact ⟨y, by rw [freeEff, cleanup_get, freeS_get, hy]; simp only [Option.map_some, hn,
635	    ↓reduceIte, hl], ya⟩
636	
637	/-- After `free p`, no active authority covers a leaf of the released unit, and every active
638	authority has a live holder (§70 `ok` effect, §54). -/
639	theorem free_no_dangling {k : K} {s s' : S3} {p auth : Nat} (h : FreeStep k p auth s (.ok s')) :
640	    ∀ (j : Nat) (y : Authority), s'.A[j]? = some y → y.active = true →
641	      (∀ l ∈ y.footprint, ¬ FreedPlace s.P p l) ∧ HolderLive s' y.holder := by
642	  obtain ⟨-, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 h
643	  intro j y hy ya
644	  obtain ⟨-, hc, hl⟩ := free_active hy ya
645	  exact ⟨fun l hl' hf => hc (.inl ⟨l, hl', hf⟩),
646	    (HolderLive.congr (s := freeS s p) (s' := freeEff s p) rfl rfl rfl _).2 hl⟩
647	
648	/-- `free` preserves `NoDangling` (§54, §70), under `WF3` (§49) and `I1` (§50): an active
649	authority on a leaf of a place that stops being usable is derived, and blocked by §70.3, or a
650	root, held by the owner of the root place of the leaf (`rootHeldConv_active`), which would stay
651	usable. -/
652	theorem EndFree.free_noDangling {k : K} {s : S3} {p auth : Nat} (hw : WF3 s) (hnd : NoDangling s)
653	    (h1 : I1 s) (hpre : FreePre k s p auth) (hw' : WF3 (freeEff s p)) :
654	    NoDangling (freeEff s p) := by
655	  have hU := cleanup_usable (freeS s p)
656	  intro j z hz za q hq l hl hlz
657	  obtain ⟨hz₀, hnc, hlive⟩ := free_active hz za
658	  by_cases hq₀ : ¬ s.Usable q
659	  · exact hnd j z hz₀ za q hq₀ l hl hlz
660	  replace hq₀ := Decidable.of_not_not hq₀
661	  obtain ⟨-, hleaf, hlq⟩ := mem_footprint.1 hl
662	  have hl₀ : s.Usable l := usable_of_partOf hw (l + 1) l q (Nat.lt_succ_self l) hlq hq₀
663	  have hl₁ : ¬ (freeS s p).Usable l := fun hu => hq (usable_of_part hw' hlq ((hU l).2 hu))
664	  cases hzo : z.origin with
665	  | some o =>
666	    have hacc := hpre.access j (List.mem_range.2 (lt_of_getElem? hz₀))
667	    unfold FreeAccessOK OptP at hacc; rw [hz₀] at hacc
668	    rcases hacc za (by rw [hzo]; simp) ⟨l, hlz, .inr ⟨hleaf, hl₀, hl₁⟩⟩ with e | e
669	    · exact hnc (.inr e)
670	    · exact e hlive
671	  | none =>
672	    obtain ⟨-, -, r, -, -, -, hr, hlr, -⟩ := hw.rootChain j z l hz₀ hlz hleaf
673	    obtain ⟨pr, hpr, hh⟩ := rootHeldConv_active hw h1 hnd j z l r hz₀ za hzo hlz hr hlr
674	    have hnf : ¬ FreedPlace s.P p r := by
675	      rintro (hrp | hown)
676	      · obtain rfl := eq_of_partOf_root hr hrp
677	        exact hnc (.inl ⟨l, hlz, .inl hlr⟩)
678	      · cases hown with
679	        | @direct _ o _ hpl ho hpart =>
680	          have e : pr.owner = .place o := by rw [hpr] at hpl; cases hpl; exact ho
681	          rw [hh, e] at hnc; exact hnc (.inr hpart)
682	        | @step _ o _ hpl ho hown' =>
683	          have e : pr.owner = .place o := by rw [hpr] at hpl; cases hpl; exact ho
684	          rw [hh, e] at hlive
685	          have := dead_false hlive
686	          simp only [freeS, Bool.or_eq_false_iff, decide_eq_false_iff_not] at this
687	          exact this.2 (.inr hown')
688	    have hd : (freeS s p).dead r = false := by
689	      simp only [freeS, ← hw.deadOf hlr, dead_false hl₀, Bool.false_or, decide_eq_false_iff_not]
690	      exact hnf
691	    have hr₁ : (freeS s p).Usable r := usable_of_owner hpr hd (hh ▸ hlive)
692	    exact hl₁ ((hU l).1 (usable_of_partOf hw' (l + 1) l r (Nat.lt_succ_self l) hlr ((hU r).2 hr₁)))
693	
694	/-- `free` preserves the kernel invariant `KInv` (§57) (O13, §70). -/
695	theorem free_preserves {k : K} {s s' : S3} {p auth : Nat} (hk : KInv s)
696	    (h : FreeStep k p auth s (.ok s')) : KInv s' := by
697	  obtain ⟨hpre, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 h
698	  have hw := hk.1
699	  have hroot := rootPlace_of_ownedRoot hpre.ownedRoot
700	  refine releases_preserve hk (freeS_releases s p) rfl rfl rfl
701	    (fun q h => by simp only [freeS, Bool.or_eq_false_iff] at h; exact h.1)
702	    (fun q pl r hq hp => ?_) (fun q _ x hx => hx) (free_anchors hk.2.1.1.2.2.1 hpre)
703	    (fun r i z pr hrp hur hz _ _ hpr hzh hzf => ?_)
704	    (free_noDangling hw hk.2.1.2.2 hk.2.1.1.1 hpre)
705	  · obtain ⟨pr, hpr, hlt, -, hd⟩ := hw.places q pl r hq hp
706	    have hpo : parentOf s.P q = some r := by simp [parentOf, hq, hp]
707	    have hf : FreedPlace s.P p r ↔ FreedPlace s.P p q := by
708	      unfold FreedPlace
709	      rw [partOf_parent hpo hlt (lt_of_getElem? hpr) hroot.2, ownedIn_parent hw hq hp]
710	    simp only [freeS, hd, decide_eq_decide.2 hf]
711	  · have hnf : ¬ FreedPlace s.P p r := fun hf => by
712	      have := dead_false hur
713	      simp only [freeS, Bool.or_eq_false_iff, decide_eq_false_iff_not] at this
714	      exact this.2 hf
715	    have hc : ¬ ((∃ l ∈ z.footprint, FreedPlace s.P p l) ∨ heldIn s.P p z.holder) := by
716	      rintro (⟨l, hl, hfl⟩ | hh)
717	      · obtain ⟨-, -, hlr⟩ := mem_footprint.1 ((hzf l).1 hl)
718	        rcases hfl with hlp | hown
719	        · obtain rfl := rootOf_unique hrp hroot hlr hlp
720	          exact hnf (.inl ⟨hroot.1, .inl rfl⟩)
721	        · obtain ⟨pl, pr', hpl, hpr', ho⟩ := hw.ownerOf hlr
722	          exact hnf (.inr (ownedIn_of_owner hpl hpr' ho.symm hown))
723	      · rw [hzh] at hh
724	        cases ho : pr.owner with
725	        | frame f => rw [ho] at hh; exact hh
726	        | place o => rw [ho] at hh; exact hnf (.inr (.direct hpr ho hh))
727	    rw [freeS_get, hz]; simp [hc]
728	
729	/-- `free` preserves the auxiliary `KAux` (`RootHeldConv`, §40, §49.7; O13, §70 `ok` effect:
730	places are unchanged and authorities are only released). -/
731	theorem free_preserves_kAux {k : K} {s s' : S3} {p auth : Nat} (ha : KAux s)
732	    (h : FreeStep k p auth s (.ok s')) : KAux s' := by
733	  obtain ⟨-, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 h
734	  exact releases_preserve_kAux ha (freeS_releases s p) rfl
735

737	transitively, is marked dead and is not usable (§70 `ok` effect). -/
738	theorem free_unit_dead {k : K} {s s' : S3} {p auth q : Nat} (h : FreeStep k p auth s (.ok s'))
739	    (hq : FreedPlace s.P p q) : s'.dead q = true ∧ ¬ s'.Usable q := by
740	  obtain ⟨-, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 h
741	  have hd : (freeEff s p).dead q = true := by simp [freeEff, cleanup, freeS, hq]
742	  exact ⟨hd, fun hu => by rw [dead_false hu] at hd; cases hd⟩
743	
744	/-- A leaf of the released unit is a place (§70). -/
745	theorem EndFree.freedLeaf_lt {s : S3} {p l : Nat} (h : FreedLeaf s p l) : l < s.P.length := by
746	  rcases h with h | ⟨-, h, -⟩
747	  · exact (mem_footprint.1 h).1
748	  · exact h.lt
749	
750	/-- A leaf of a usable place of the released unit, a part of `p` or storage it owns
751	transitively, belongs to the released unit (§70.4), under `WF3` (§49). -/
752	theorem freedLeaf_of_unit {s : S3} (hw : WF3 s) {p q l : Nat} (hq : FreedPlace s.P p q)
753	    (hu : s.Usable q) (hl : l ∈ footprint s.P q) : FreedLeaf s p l := by
754	  rcases hq with hq | hq
755	  · exact .inl (footprint_sub hw hq hl)
756	  obtain ⟨-, hleaf, hlq⟩ := mem_footprint.1 hl
757	  refine .inr ⟨hleaf, usable_of_partOf hw (l + 1) l q (Nat.lt_succ_self l) hlq hu, fun hu' => ?_⟩
758	  obtain ⟨pl, pq, hpl, hpq, ho⟩ := hw.ownerOf hlq
759	  have := dead_false hu'
760	  simp only [freeS, Bool.or_eq_false_iff, decide_eq_false_iff_not] at this
761	  exact this.2 (.inr (ownedIn_of_owner hpq hpl ho hq))
762	
763	/-- A pinned leaf of the released unit blocks `free` (§70.4): statically (`K.Pinned`) or
764	dynamically pinned, the outcome is `reject`. -/
765	theorem free_pinned_reject {k : K} {s : S3} {p auth l : Nat} {o : Outcome3 S3}
766	    (hl : FreedLeaf s p l) (hpin : s.pin l = true ∨ k.Pinned l) (h : FreeStep k p auth s o) :
767	    o = .reject := by
768	  cases h with
769	  | ok hpre =>
770	    have hn := hpre.notPinned l (List.mem_range.2 (freedLeaf_lt hl)) hl
771	    rcases hpin with e | e
772	    · rw [hn.1] at e; cases e
773	    · exact absurd e hn.2
774	  | reject _ => rfl
775	
776	/-- `free` has one outcome (§58). -/
777	theorem free_det {k : K} {p auth : Nat} {s : S3} {o₁ o₂ : Outcome3 S3}
778	    (h₁ : FreeStep k p auth s o₁) (h₂ : FreeStep k p auth s o₂) : o₁ = o₂ := Guarded.det h₁ h₂
779	
780	/-- The `ok` outcome of `free` (§58, §70): the preconditions hold and the state is the
781	effect. -/
782	theorem free_ok_iff {k : K} {p auth : Nat} {s s' : S3} :
783	    FreeStep k p auth s (.ok s') ↔ FreePre k s p auth ∧ s' = freeEff s p := Guarded.ok_iff

# ERN — Memory Model Specification v0.1

**Edition v0.1 — corrective candidate, not yet validated**

Modified clauses, relative to v0 (each change is justified by a defect found while formalizing v0):

- §36: `MetaRight` governs authorities over existing storage, not the fresh allocation of `alloc`; §36 and §71.2 contradicted each other.

- §51: a valid origin is an active origin; "valid" was undefined there.
- §57: definition of I5, which v0 named without defining.
- §59: "access operations" are O9–O11; read as all operations, §59 contradicted §69.
- §60.1: a valid origin chain is an active one, read through §44.
- §63.4: the active derived authorities covering the source from outside are named, and the authorities through which the step exercises its `Modify` right are exempt; without this exemption no value could be moved through a derived authority.
- §63.9 (new): the destination is usable in the resulting state; without it an accepted transfer could create an ownership cycle and break §49.8 and §57.
- §69.2 and §70.3: the same exemption as §63.4, and rejection when an authority made inactive by the step keeps an active descendant; without it an accepted step left an active authority with an inactive origin.
- §71.2: the provider is a usable place; v0 did not require it to exist.
- §74 and §75: each `pin` installs an obligation of fresh identity and `unpin` ends one designated obligation; per-leaf pin flags let an `unpin` lift a pin installed by another `pin`.
- §76.6: the reading of the precondition (whole kernel state, `ArenaInv` of the new entry, resulting state); v0 admitted several readings with different verdicts.
- §78.3: restricted to anchors covering a leaf of the administered storage; as written, its second sentence was false.
- §82.2: address and provenance of a pointer to a region whose leaves all have zero physical size; v0 decided no address for that region.
- §86: the last sentence is rewritten; as written, it was false, since `reset` and `issue` leave a recycled leaf `Init` and readable.

**Higher normative authority:** *ERN — Language Charter v0* (October 27, 2026).  
This specification defines the normative rules of ERN's memory model. Technical names (`derive`, `transfer`, `issue`, etc.) designate **abstract semantic operations**; they do not constitute syntax decisions.

## Validation and Revision Procedure

This edition has been validated and acquires normative authority under the ERN Charter v0. Any subsequent semantic change must identify the clauses concerned, justify the change, and preserve the guarantees of the ERN Charter v0. Formal models and proofs are instruments for verifying this specification, not sources of additional rules. Behaviors not determined within its scope are explicitly identified.

## Scope

This specification defines:

- the safe-code contract;
- the abstract machine for allocations, bytes, and accesses;
- the second-class access discipline;
- footprints, authorities, dependencies, frames, and ownership;
- read, write, transfer, release, allocation, and pinning transitions;
- the normative contract of arenas as a reference library abstraction;
- the correspondence obligations between these mechanisms.

It does not define syntax, the complete concurrency model, control-flow conventions, the type system, or compiler lowering. The sequential model's scope does not waive the general guarantees of the Charter.

---

----
## 40. Logical Places, Leaves, and Ownership

A place has an identity, optionally a structural parent, an abstract `kind`, an owner `owner : Frame | Place`, and a logical death marker. Structural parenthood `partOf(p,q)` describes the subplaces of a value; `owner` describes **who keeps the storage** of a root place valid. An owned place may lie outside its owner's direct footprint; ownership and composition are therefore distinct.

A **leaf** is a place with no structural children. `footprint(p)` contains the leaves of `p`, and access rights over a place are evaluated on those leaves. Places transitively owned by a value are not automatically leaves of its `footprint`. A logical unit of the access discipline does not automatically constitute an additional allocation in the elementary memory machine.

A place `p` is **usable** (`Usable(s,p)`) if and only if:

1. `p` exists and is not marked dead;
2. if its owner is a frame, that frame belongs to the stack;
3. if its owner is a place `q`, then `q` is itself usable and the chain terminates at a frame in the stack.

An ownership cycle makes no place usable. `placeFrame(p)` is the terminal frame of this chain when `p` is usable. Structural parts share their parent's owner and death marker. A value may be logically ended by `endUse` without the place that contained it becoming unusable; the substorages it owned may, however, die.

A **root place** has no structural parent. Every **usable** root place has a root authority of own mode `Modify`, with no origin, held exactly by that place's owner (`RootHeld`). This authority cannot be transferred in isolation; root ownership follows a legal transfer of the owning value when necessary.

## 41. Leaf Initialization States

Every tracked leaf has exactly one of the states `Uninit`, `Init`, or `Moved`.

- `Uninit`: no initialized value available in this leaf.
- `Init`: initialized value, subject to type, representation, and storage obligations.
- `Moved`: value consumed by transfer, inaccessible as its former value.

Aggregates may be partially initialized. Both `Uninit` and `Moved` prohibit ordinary reads, while remaining distinct states for diagnostics and end-of-use obligations. An initialization state creates no access permission.

## 42. Authorities, Modes, Holders, and Origins

An authority conceptually has the following fields:

```text
Authority {
    id
    mode: Observe | Modify
    origin?: AuthorityId
    footprint: Set<Leaf>
    holder: Frame | Place
    active: Bool
}
```

`origin` links a derived authority to its current origin. Authorities have fresh identities and well-formed origin chains. A root authority has no origin; a derived authority has one. Creating derived rights does not increase the scope or permitted mode of the origin.

The **holder** (`holder`) is not the **owner** (`owner`). An authority derived by `derive` or `split` is initially held by the current frame; `store` or a permitted transfer may make it held by a place. The derived `issue` operation proceeds through `split` followed by `store`. `release` does not release a root. There is no persistent `Suspended` field: suspension of rights is inferred from active descendants and applies leaf by leaf.

## 43. Effective Rights and Exercise of Authorities

For an authority `a` and a leaf `l`, `effective(s,a,l)` is derived from the active descendants of `a` whose footprint contains `l`:

1. if `a` is inactive or does not cover `l`, its effective mode is absent;
2. if no active descendant covers `l`, the effective mode is the own mode of `a`;
3. if an active descendant with own mode `Modify` covers `l`, the effective mode of `a` is absent;
4. otherwise, when the covering active descendants are `Observe`, the effective mode of `a` on `l` is `Observe`.

The effect is **local to each leaf**: after splitting a region, the origin may retain effective `Modify` over undistributed leaves.

Requested modes are ordered `Observe ≤ Modify`. `ExercisableAt(s,a,m)` means:

- `a` is active and its own mode permits `m`;
- either `a` is held by the current frame;
- or `a` is held by a place `p`, and the current frame has, over **all** leaves of `p`, an authority itself exercisable in mode `m` with sufficient effective mode.

The latter clause is recursive along the holder chain. Thus, being active or covering a leaf does not automatically make an authority exercisable. `HasRight(s,m,p)` means the current frame has exercise in mode `m` and sufficient effective mode **over every leaf in `p`'s footprint**. Every operation requires the modes it actually needs; an authority's own mode alone is insufficient.

## 44. Dependencies and Effective Anchors

`D(p)` is the set of authorities serving as **validity anchors** for place `p`. An anchor is valid as long as the authority it names is active. Dependencies of contained values are accounted for transitively. Relevant dependencies follow the value during transfer; those of its container do not automatically follow a part transferred in isolation.

For an authority `x`, its **effective anchor** is the root reached by traversing its origin chain. It does not necessarily coincide with its current holder. Lifetime constraints are calculated from the frame of that effective anchor and the frames of places that remain usable. A dependency cannot create a right or artificially extend a lifetime.

`AnchorOrder` requires, for every anchor `x ∈ D(q)` of a usable place `q`, that the frame of the effective anchor of `x` be the frame of `q` or one of its ancestors. `AnchorOrderHeld` imposes the same rule on every **active authority held** by `q`. These conditions apply to the resulting states of operations that move or create holder relations.

## 45. Parameters, Returns, and Reanchoring

A call parameter is an **active derived authority held by the caller** before being passed to the callee; its original provenance may go back to an earlier frame. This interpretation does not require that the authority was originally derived in the calling frame; that additional requirement belongs to Spec 3. The caller **yields** the authority to the new frame: it does not simultaneously retain a copy. If the authority remains in that frame upon return, `exitFrame` releases it; **it is not automatically returned to the caller**. To retain its own right, the caller may pass a **fresh derivative** of the authority it wishes to keep: this is ordinary reborrowing. The definition of ergonomic calling conventions is deferred to Spec 3.

## 49. WF3 — Well-Formedness of Frames, Places, and Authorities

`WF3(s)` is a **predicate on state `s`**. It jointly requires:

1. a nonempty, duplicate-free frame stack, every frame having a valid identity and, except for the base frame, a valid parent; frame-parent relations are well-founded;
2. a place structure whose composition links are valid and **acyclic**; every structural part shares its parent's owner and death marker;
3. valid owners of type frame or place, and **well-founded** ownership chains reaching a live frame for every usable place;
4. footprints consisting exclusively of leaves of existing places;
5. authorities with valid identities and modes, whose existing origins form **acyclic** chains ending at a root authority;
6. `RootChain`: every origin chain of an authority covering a leaf ends at the root of the **same structural root place** as that leaf;
7. `RootHeld`: every usable root place has its active root `Modify` authority, with no origin, held exactly by its owner;
8. holder validity: every active authority is held by a frame present in the stack or by a usable place.

Numerical ordering of identifiers, parent precedence over child in a list, and bounds on generated identifiers may be used **to represent or prove** this well-formedness in a formalization; they are not normative restrictions on place or authority identities. Preservation of `WF3` by a transition is a **required property of transitions**, not an additional clause of the state predicate. `WF3` does not impose any particular physical object layout: that belongs to refinement into the elementary memory machine.

## 50. I1 — Structural Exclusivity

For two active authorities **unrelated by derivation** covering the same leaf, their own modes must both be `Observe`. This rule also applies to leaves identified as `SharedMutable`; their particular mutation is governed by the `writeShared` contract and creates no exception to I1.

Exclusivity of **effective** modes (`effective_exclusive`) is a consequence of I1 and the definition of `effective`, not the definition of I1. On a leaf, two incompatible authorities cannot simultaneously possess incompatible effective rights. The only permitted independent ordinary coexistence is `Observe` / `Observe`.

## 51. I2 — Conservation of Rights

A derived authority covers only a subfootprint of what its origin chain permits and does not elevate its mode. Derivation and splitting restrictions do not allow duplication of an exclusive right over a leaf. Every active authority is linked to a valid origin according to state and reanchoring rules: an origin is **valid** if and only if it is active, so the origin of an active derived authority is active. Partial suspension follows from `effective`.

## 52. I3 — Validity of Anchors and Dependencies

Every explicit anchor of a still-usable place is valid. An operation cannot invalidate an anchor retained by a place that remains usable. Transitive propagation of dependencies from contained values does not change this obligation. Dependencies are not permissions and are insufficient to justify an access.

## 53. I4 — Consumption and Movement

A `Moved` leaf cannot be read as if it still contained its previous value. Moving a value does not preserve two copies of an exclusive authority. Initialization state and authority-exercise state are separate checks.

## 54. Anchor Ordering and Absence of Orphan Rights

`AnchorOrder` and `AnchorOrderHeld` are defined in Section 44. `NoDangling` prohibits an **active** authority from covering a leaf belonging to an unusable place; the invariant does not say that a leaf is initialized. `NoOrphan` requires every active authority held by a place to be connected to a frame in the stack through a **finite, non-repeating chain** of authorities: the first link is held by a live frame, and each active link **structurally covers the entirety** of the place holding the next link. The link need not have an effective mode over that place. `NoOrphan` guarantees neither the exercisability of all stored authorities nor freedom from blocking.

## 55. ArenaInv — Invariant of the Arena Abstraction

`ArenaInv` is an invariant of the **library contract**, not an additional predicate of kernel state. For every live arena:

- `storage` designates an existing, usable place; the footprint of `internal` is exactly the footprint of `storage`;
- `internal` is active, with own mode `Modify`, held by the arena value;
- available leaves and issued regions belong to the administered storage;
- two still-active issuances have disjoint regions; no leaf of a still-issued region simultaneously belongs to `available`;
- every still-issued block authority is a derivative of `internal` complying with exclusivity and validity rules;
- anchor and ownership restrictions are respected.

Arena entries do not, by themselves, constitute an additional storage owner. Two live arenas may cover common leaves when their `internal` authorities are distinct and their effective rights are compatible; no **global** disjointness of arena footprints is imposed.

## 56. Uniqueness of Live Administration

**An authority identity may serve as `internal` for at most one live administrative abstraction**, whether an arena, `HandlePool`, `DataStack`, or another library administrative instance. Before registering a new abstraction, its creation operation must jointly check the absence of that identity from **all relevant registries of live administrations**. Uniqueness concerns the identity of the `internal` authority, not merely possible overlap of footprints: abstractions with distinct `internal` identities are not forbidden merely because their footprints overlap. Library contracts must make the information required for this guard available to the creation operation; checking only an abstraction's own registry is insufficient.

**This guard is not a condition for any safety property in Section 57.** The effective right (Section 43, case 3) already prohibits a second issuance over leaves covered by an active block derived from the same authority. Rather, the guard preserves the **abstraction contract**: without it, simultaneous administration of the same `internal` could cause `reject` instead of `fail`, or reissue a previously released block that the first administration still considers unavailable. It creates neither permissions nor allocations and introduces no general detection of authority cycles. Its physical representation and encapsulation of library registries remain outside the kernel.

## 57. Main Invariant

\[
Inv3 = I1 \land I2 \land I3 \land I4 \land AnchorOrder \land NoDangling
\]

On states reachable from `S3.init statics` under `DDSound(K)`, the kernel guarantees:

\[
WF3 \land Inv3 \land AnchorOrderHeld \land NoOrphan
\]

`ArenaInv` (Section 55) belongs to the library abstraction: it is not included in this main kernel invariant.

**I5:** every pinned leaf, statically (`K.Pinned`) or dynamically (an active pinning obligation, Section 74), belongs to a usable place.

I5, associated with pinned storage, remains a **specialized obligation** of `K.Pinned`, not a clause automatically implied by sequential accesses alone. This property is required for reachable states under the declared assumptions. Its correspondence with allocations and bytes requires the refinement defined below.

----
## 69. O12 — Logical End of a Value's Use

**Preconditions**

1. `place` is usable and the current frame has exercisable `Modify` over it.
2. No active descendant over the leaves of `place` **or storage that dies with it** is held outside the places dying with `place`, in a way that would prevent rights from returning or being invalidated. The authorities through which the step exercises its `Modify` right over `place`, namely the exercisable authority on which that right rests and its origin chain, are exempt from this check. Moreover, no authority that the effect makes inactive (held by `place` or by a place dying with it, transitively owned storage included) has an active descendant, whatever its footprint, that the same step does not make inactive.
3. No place **remaining usable after the effect** depends on an authority held by `place`, its root, or an authority that would become inactive when an owned holder dies.
4. **No leaf whose use ends, including transitively owned storage, is pinned**, either statically (`K.Pinned`) or dynamically (`pin`). A dynamic pinning obligation must be legally removed by `unpin` before this step.

**`ok` effect:** The leaves of value `place` become `Uninit`; `place` **remains usable as a place** and may legally be reinitialized. Authorities held by `place` and dead substorages are released; dependencies of the ended value are removed; transitively owned places that cease to live are marked dead. The operation does not automatically trigger physical deallocation in the elementary memory machine: an unfreed allocation may constitute a leak, which this guarantee does not prohibit. **Other outcome:** `reject`.

## 70. O13 — Release of an Owned Storage Unit

**Preconditions**

1. `place` is a **root of storage owned by a value** (`OwnedRoot`), not an ordinary local directly owned by a frame and not part of an aggregate.
2. `K.Deallocable(place)` is established, and `K.FreeCompat(place,auth)` justifies deallocation authority `auth`; this identifier is opaque to the authority kernel.
3. The current frame has exercisable `Modify`; no active derivative over the footprint being freed is held outside holders that die; no surviving place is anchored to an authority of the released region or of its dead holders. The authorities through which the step exercises its `Modify` right over `place`, namely the exercisable authority on which that right rests and its origin chain, are exempt from the check on active derivatives. Moreover, no authority that the effect makes inactive (an authority of the released region, its root included, or an authority whose holder dies) has an active descendant, whatever its footprint, that the same step does not make inactive.
4. No leaf of the released unit is statically or dynamically pinned. Ending external use does not silently turn a still-pinned leaf into a releasable unit.

**`ok` effect:** `place` and the storage that ceases to live are marked dead; authorities of those regions, including their corresponding roots, become inactive, as do authorities whose holders die. Surviving dependencies must remain valid. Every realization of `free` must satisfy the corresponding deallocation relation of the elementary memory machine (Part III). **Other outcome:** `reject`.

----
## 74. O15 — Dynamic Pinning

**Preconditions:** `place` is usable, the current frame has exercisable `Modify` over the relevant leaves, and the operation respects applicable pinning obligations.

**`ok` effect:** A dynamic pinning obligation of fresh identity is installed on the relevant leaves. A leaf is dynamically pinned while at least one active pinning obligation covers it. While an obligation is active, `transfer`, `endUse`, `free`, and `exitFrame` are rejected if they act on leaves it pins; removal of this obligation requires `unpin` under `K.ExternalDone`. Pinning does not make contents immutable. **Other outcome:** `reject`.

## 75. O16 — Removal of Dynamic Pinning

**Preconditions:** `unpin` designates one active dynamic pinning obligation, installed by `pin` on `place`; `place` is usable, the current frame has exercisable `Modify`, and contract `K.ExternalDone`, applied to that obligation, attests that all relevant external use has ended.

**`ok` effect:** The designated dynamic pinning obligation ends, and only that one: a leaf it covered stays pinned while another active obligation covers it. The step does not itself modify values, their initialization, or their access authorities. Static obligations are not removed by this operation. **Other outcome:** `reject`.

**Associated static rule (`StaticPinnedBottom`):** Statics designated by `K.Pinned` must be places **directly** owned by the **base frame**, not merely transitively owned by a static value. This restriction ensures that they do not die when an intermediate frame exits.

# XIV. Arenas and Collective Invalidation — Reference Abstraction

An arena is a **library abstraction**, not a memory-kernel primitive. Operations O17 through O19 are **derived** from operations O1 through O16 and abstraction-specific metadata: `newArena` registers an administration without modifying the kernel; `issue` performs `split` followed by `store` (after checking availability); `reset` performs a `Modify` derivation over all storage—through `derive` or `split`—then `release`, before restoring availability. Their contract below is **normative for the standard-library arena** until Spec 10 takes responsibility for it. It authorizes neither new permissions nor an additional access machine. Arena entries (Section 46) constitute the abstract state of this administration; the guard in Section 56 belongs to its consistency contract. The contracts of `HandlePool` and `DataStack` belong to their library abstractions and are not defined here.

/-- Releases every authority whose holder is no longer live (§69, §70 `ok` effects). -/
def cleanup (s : S3) : S3 :=
  { s with A := s.A.map fun y => if HolderLive s y.holder then y else { y with active := false } }

/-! ## O12 `endUse` (§69) -/

/-- `endUse p` before releasing authorities whose holder died (§69, `ok` effect): the leaves of
`p` become `Uninit`; authorities held within `p` are released; anchors of `p` and its parts are
removed; storage owned by `p`, transitively, is marked dead. -/
def endUseS (s : S3) (p : Nat) : S3 :=
  { s with
    I := fun l => if l ∈ footprint s.P p then .uninit else s.I l
    D := fun q => if partOf s.P q p then [] else s.D q
    dead := fun q => s.dead q || decide (OwnedIn s.P p q)
    A := s.A.map fun y => if heldIn s.P p y.holder then { y with active := false } else y }

/-- Effect of `endUse p` (§69, `ok` effect): `endUseS`, then the authorities whose holder died
are released. -/
def endUseEff (s : S3) (p : Nat) : S3 := cleanup (endUseS s p)

/-- Leaf whose use ends with the value at `p` (§69.2, §69.4): a leaf of `p` or of storage that
stops being usable. -/
def EndingLeaf (s : S3) (p l : Nat) : Prop :=
  l ∈ footprint s.P p ∨ (isLeaf s.P l ∧ s.Usable l ∧ ¬ (endUseS s p).Usable l)

/-- Decidability of `EndingLeaf` (§69). -/
instance (s : S3) (p l : Nat) : Decidable (EndingLeaf s p l) := by
  unfold EndingLeaf; infer_instance

/-- Root authority of the value at `p` (§69.3): an authority with no origin covering a leaf of
`p`. -/
def IsRootOf (s : S3) (p : Nat) (y : Authority) : Prop :=
  y.origin = none ∧ ∃ l ∈ footprint s.P p, l ∈ y.footprint

/-- Decidability of `IsRootOf` (§69.3). -/
instance (s : S3) (p : Nat) (y : Authority) : Decidable (IsRootOf s p y) := by
  unfold IsRootOf; infer_instance

/-- Authority `j` does not block `endUse p` (§69.2): if it is an active derived authority over an
ending leaf, it is held within `p` or its holder dies. -/
def EndUseAccessOK (s : S3) (p j : Nat) : Prop :=
  OptP (s.A[j]?) (fun y => y.active = true → y.origin ≠ none →
    (∃ l ∈ y.footprint, EndingLeaf s p l) →
      heldIn s.P p y.holder ∨ ¬ HolderLive (endUseS s p) y.holder) True

/-- Decidability of `EndUseAccessOK` (§69.2). -/
instance (s : S3) (p j : Nat) : Decidable (EndUseAccessOK s p j) := by
  unfold EndUseAccessOK OptP; split <;> infer_instance

/-- Anchor `x` survives `endUse p` (§69.3): not held within `p`, not a root of `p`, with a holder
that stays live. -/
def EndUseAnchorOK (s : S3) (p x : Nat) : Prop :=
  OptP (s.A[x]?) (fun y => ¬ heldIn s.P p y.holder ∧ ¬ IsRootOf s p y ∧
    HolderLive (endUseS s p) y.holder) True

/-- Decidability of `EndUseAnchorOK` (§69.3). -/
instance (s : S3) (p x : Nat) : Decidable (EndUseAnchorOK s p x) := by
  unfold EndUseAnchorOK OptP; split <;> infer_instance

/-- Preconditions of `endUse` (§69). -/
structure EndUsePre (k : K) (s : S3) (p : Nat) : Prop where
  /-- §69.1: `place` is usable. -/
  usable : s.Usable p
  /-- §69.1: exercisable `Modify` over `place`. -/
  right : HasRight s .modify p
  /-- §69.2: no active derived authority over an ending leaf is held outside the dying places,
  except the authorities through which the step exercises its `Modify` right over `place`: some
  authority grounding that right and its origin chain. -/
  access : ∃ g ∈ List.range s.A.length, Grounds s .modify p g ∧
    ∀ j ∈ List.range s.A.length, RightChain s g j ∨ EndUseAccessOK s p j
  /-- §69.2, last sentence: no authority that the effect makes inactive has an active descendant
  that the effect does not make inactive. -/
  keptDesc : ∀ a ∈ List.range s.A.length, ∀ j ∈ List.range s.A.length, s.Active a →
    ¬ (endUseEff s p).Active a → a ∈ s.ancs j → ¬ (endUseEff s p).Active j
  /-- §69.3: no place usable after the effect depends on an authority held by `place`, its root,
  or an authority whose holder dies. -/
  anchors : ∀ q ∈ List.range s.P.length, (endUseS s p).Usable q →
    ∀ x ∈ (endUseS s p).D q, EndUseAnchorOK s p x
  /-- §69.4: no ending leaf, owned storage included, is pinned, statically or dynamically. -/
  notPinned : ∀ l ∈ List.range s.P.length, EndingLeaf s p l → s.pin l = false ∧ ¬ k.Pinned l

/-- Decidability of the preconditions of `endUse` (§69). -/
instance (k : K) [DecidablePred k.Pinned] (s : S3) (p : Nat) : Decidable (EndUsePre k s p) :=
  decidable_of_iff (s.Usable p ∧ HasRight s .modify p ∧
    (∃ g ∈ List.range s.A.length, Grounds s .modify p g ∧
      ∀ j ∈ List.range s.A.length, RightChain s g j ∨ EndUseAccessOK s p j) ∧
    (∀ a ∈ List.range s.A.length, ∀ j ∈ List.range s.A.length, s.Active a →
      ¬ (endUseEff s p).Active a → a ∈ s.ancs j → ¬ (endUseEff s p).Active j) ∧
    (∀ q ∈ List.range s.P.length, (endUseS s p).Usable q →
      ∀ x ∈ (endUseS s p).D q, EndUseAnchorOK s p x) ∧
    (∀ l ∈ List.range s.P.length, EndingLeaf s p l → s.pin l = false ∧ ¬ k.Pinned l))
    ⟨fun ⟨a, b, c, d, e, f⟩ => ⟨a, b, c, d, e, f⟩, fun ⟨a, b, c, d, e, f⟩ => ⟨a, b, c, d, e, f⟩⟩

/-- `endUse` as a relation (§69). -/
def EndUseStep (k : K) (p : Nat) (s : S3) : Outcome3 S3 → Prop :=
  Guarded (EndUsePre k s p) (endUseEff s p)

/-! ## O13 `free` (§70) -/

/-- The holder is a place (§70.1). -/
def Holder.isPlace : Holder → Bool
  | .place _ => true
  | .frame _ => false

/-- `OwnedRoot` (§70.1): a place with no structural parent, owned by a place. -/
def OwnedRoot (s : S3) (p : Nat) : Prop :=
  OptP (s.P[p]?) (fun pl => pl.parent = none ∧ pl.owner.isPlace = true) False

/-- Decidability of `OwnedRoot` (§70.1). -/
instance (s : S3) (p : Nat) : Decidable (OwnedRoot s p) := by
  unfold OwnedRoot; infer_instance

/-- Place `q` belongs to the unit released by `free p` (§70): a part of `p`, or storage owned by
`p`, transitively. -/
def FreedPlace (P : List Place) (p q : Nat) : Prop := partOf P q p ∨ OwnedIn P p q

/-- Decidability of `FreedPlace` (§70). -/
instance (P : List Place) (p q : Nat) : Decidable (FreedPlace P p q) := by
  unfold FreedPlace; infer_instance

/-- `free p` before releasing authorities whose holder died (§70, `ok` effect): the released unit
is marked dead; authorities covering it, roots included, or held within `p` become inactive. -/
def freeS (s : S3) (p : Nat) : S3 :=
  { s with
    dead := fun q => s.dead q || decide (FreedPlace s.P p q)
    A := s.A.map fun y =>
      if (∃ l ∈ y.footprint, FreedPlace s.P p l) ∨ heldIn s.P p y.holder then
        { y with active := false } else y }

/-- Effect of `free p` (§70, `ok` effect): `freeS`, then the authorities whose holder died are
released. -/
def freeEff (s : S3) (p : Nat) : S3 := cleanup (freeS s p)

/-- Leaf of the released unit (§70.3, §70.4): a leaf of `p` or of storage that stops being
usable. -/
def FreedLeaf (s : S3) (p l : Nat) : Prop :=
  l ∈ footprint s.P p ∨ (isLeaf s.P l ∧ s.Usable l ∧ ¬ (freeS s p).Usable l)

/-- Decidability of `FreedLeaf` (§70). -/
instance (s : S3) (p l : Nat) : Decidable (FreedLeaf s p l) := by
  unfold FreedLeaf; infer_instance

/-- Authority `j` does not block `free p` (§70.3): if it is an active derivative over the
footprint being freed, it is held within `p` or its holder dies. -/
def FreeAccessOK (s : S3) (p j : Nat) : Prop :=
  OptP (s.A[j]?) (fun y => y.active = true → y.origin ≠ none →
    (∃ l ∈ y.footprint, FreedLeaf s p l) →
      heldIn s.P p y.holder ∨ ¬ HolderLive (freeS s p) y.holder) True

/-- Decidability of `FreeAccessOK` (§70.3). -/
instance (s : S3) (p j : Nat) : Decidable (FreeAccessOK s p j) := by
  unfold FreeAccessOK OptP; split <;> infer_instance

/-- Anchor `x` survives `free p` (§70.3): it covers no leaf of the released unit, is not held
within `p`, and its holder stays live. -/
def FreeAnchorOK (s : S3) (p x : Nat) : Prop :=
  OptP (s.A[x]?) (fun y => ¬ (∃ l ∈ y.footprint, FreedPlace s.P p l) ∧ ¬ heldIn s.P p y.holder ∧
    HolderLive (freeS s p) y.holder) True

/-- Decidability of `FreeAnchorOK` (§70.3). -/
instance (s : S3) (p x : Nat) : Decidable (FreeAnchorOK s p x) := by
  unfold FreeAnchorOK OptP; split <;> infer_instance

/-- Preconditions of `free p auth` (§70). -/
structure FreePre (k : K) (s : S3) (p auth : Nat) : Prop where
  /-- §70.1: `place` is an `OwnedRoot`. -/
  ownedRoot : OwnedRoot s p
  /-- §70.2: `K.Deallocable(place)`. -/
  deallocable : k.Deallocable p
  /-- §70.2: `K.FreeCompat(place, auth)`. -/
  freeCompat : k.FreeCompat p auth
  /-- §70.3: exercisable `Modify` over `place`. -/
  right : HasRight s .modify p
  /-- §70.3: no active derivative over the footprint being freed is held outside dying holders,
  except the authorities through which the step exercises its `Modify` right over `place`: some
  authority grounding that right and its origin chain. -/
  access : ∃ g ∈ List.range s.A.length, Grounds s .modify p g ∧
    ∀ j ∈ List.range s.A.length, RightChain s g j ∨ FreeAccessOK s p j
  /-- §70.3, last sentence: no authority that the effect makes inactive has an active descendant
  that the effect does not make inactive. -/
  keptDesc : ∀ a ∈ List.range s.A.length, ∀ j ∈ List.range s.A.length, s.Active a →
    ¬ (freeEff s p).Active a → a ∈ s.ancs j → ¬ (freeEff s p).Active j
  /-- §70.3: no surviving place is anchored to an authority of the released unit or of its dead
  holders. -/
  anchors : ∀ q ∈ List.range s.P.length, (freeS s p).Usable q → ∀ x ∈ s.D q, FreeAnchorOK s p x
  /-- §70.4: no leaf of the released unit is pinned, statically or dynamically. -/
  notPinned : ∀ l ∈ List.range s.P.length, FreedLeaf s p l → s.pin l = false ∧ ¬ k.Pinned l

/-- Decidability of the preconditions of `free` (§70). -/
instance (k : K) [DecidablePred k.Pinned] [DecidablePred k.Deallocable]
    [∀ p a, Decidable (k.FreeCompat p a)] (s : S3) (p auth : Nat) :
    Decidable (FreePre k s p auth) :=
  decidable_of_iff (OwnedRoot s p ∧ k.Deallocable p ∧ k.FreeCompat p auth ∧
    HasRight s .modify p ∧
    (∃ g ∈ List.range s.A.length, Grounds s .modify p g ∧
      ∀ j ∈ List.range s.A.length, RightChain s g j ∨ FreeAccessOK s p j) ∧
    (∀ a ∈ List.range s.A.length, ∀ j ∈ List.range s.A.length, s.Active a →
      ¬ (freeEff s p).Active a → a ∈ s.ancs j → ¬ (freeEff s p).Active j) ∧
    (∀ q ∈ List.range s.P.length, (freeS s p).Usable q → ∀ x ∈ s.D q, FreeAnchorOK s p x) ∧
    (∀ l ∈ List.range s.P.length, FreedLeaf s p l → s.pin l = false ∧ ¬ k.Pinned l))
    ⟨fun ⟨a, b, c, d, e, f, g, h⟩ => ⟨a, b, c, d, e, f, g, h⟩,
     fun ⟨a, b, c, d, e, f, g, h⟩ => ⟨a, b, c, d, e, f, g, h⟩⟩

/-- `free` as a relation (§70). -/
def FreeStep (k : K) (p auth : Nat) (s : S3) : Outcome3 S3 → Prop :=
  Guarded (FreePre k s p auth) (freeEff s p)

/-! ## O14 `alloc` (§71) -/

/-- Static preconditions of `alloc provider owner shape` (§71, items 1–3). -/
structure AllocStatic (k : K) (s : S3) (provider owner : Nat) (ls : LocalShape) : Prop where
  /-- §71.1: the shape is nonempty. -/
  nonempty : ls ≠ []
  /-- §71.1: the shape is represented like the locals of `enterFrame` (each parent is an earlier
  element). -/
  shapeOK : ShapeOK s.P.length ls.toShape
  /-- §71.1 with the `ok` outcome of §71 ("a new storage root"): exactly one element has no
  parent. -/
  oneRoot : (rootIdx ls.toShape).length = 1
  /-- §71.2: the provider is a usable place. -/
